scope: Android/Termux operational harness only; runtime implementation is indexed but not owned by this harness lane.

operatorCommands.humanScrollbackFallback: Ctrl+B then [; use PgUp/PgDn/arrows; q exits copy mode
operatorCommands.nanoExitDiscard: Ctrl+X then N when the modified buffer is accidental
operatorCommands.nanoExitSave: Ctrl+X then Y then Enter when the shown filename and prompt contents are intentional
operatorCommands.verifyClone: git rev-parse --show-toplevel && git remote get-url origin

knownTraps: Android long-press selection may visually cross tmux split panes; do not use native selection as the primary evidence boundary.
Touch scrolling may not address tmux history predictably; use bounded capture-pane for evidence and tmux copy mode only for human browsing.
A pane displaying authentication/device-code material is sensitive; do not capture it to a durable artifact or share it.
Literal [200~ before a pasted command is input framing evidence, not proof that the intended executable is absent.

A nano screen with a filename, Modified, and ^G/^O/^X shortcuts is a modal editor waiting for input, not evidence of a hung shell. Every instruction that opens a modal surface must state the expected screen and exit contract before entry.
Do not confuse the commands used to prepare a repository or launch nano with the content of sprint.md. The prompt file must contain the bounded task instructions that the coding agent should execute.
Do not fetch origin/main or create a branch until a usable local clone and expected origin have been verified.
The portable harness validator requires Python; the harness owns the Python package prerequisite rather than silently expanding the Android runtime installer.
Herdr upstream documents stable Linux/macOS binaries but does not currently claim Android/Termux support; Linux aarch64 availability is not Android compatibility proof.
Do not replace tmux, run automatic device_config mutations, or claim background persistence until same-device Herdr evidence clears the migration gates.

Repository-family status is a PowerShell probe; on Termux without PowerShell, read the agent contract and family registry locally and defer family-level status proof to hosted or PowerShell validation rather than inventing a pass.
Root SKILLS.md and TRIGGERS.md are the discovery surface; the aggregate app-composition graph must register the Android validator so Test-AppHarness cannot pass while the Android harness is broken.
Keep Git repositories under Termux HOME, not shared storage.
Generated evidence is untracked and must not contain credentials or private key material.
The harness indexes the merged Android runtime but must not mutate runtime/product files in a harness-only sprint.

buildTestDeploy.build: No separate build; JSON/Markdown/shell harness assets are tracked source.
buildTestDeploy.deploy: Merge reviewed harness changes; no implicit hook install, Android package/runtime deployment, or Herdr promotion from this lane.

proofCeiling: Maps tracked ownership, root discovery, aggregate composition, commands, modal exit contracts, Herdr migration gates and traps only; it does not prove a particular Android UI, clipboard, foreground-process health, Herdr Android compatibility, provider, model, tool invocation, repository-family status on Termux without PowerShell, or runtime mutation.
